distinguishing_features: Open-cell metallic foam integrated into the bond-coat layer as a lateral heat-spreading network
Use of existing hot-gas and gas-metal-temperature telemetry to estimate the duty cycle and interfacial thermal response
Targeted reduction of peak ceramic/bond-coat interface temperature during transient thermal cycling
Combination of transient thermal buffering with lateral thermal-gradient equalization
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce peak local temperature and steep interfacial thermal gradients in a thermally cycled turbine coating so that bond-coat oxidation and thermally induced interfacial stresses do not initiate spallation.
parsed.viable_reason: The proposed foam layer is not credible as written because a bond-coat-scale open-cell metal foam cannot realistically exhibit the asserted effective conductivity, would introduce extensive oxidation paths and stress concentrations, and cannot support the unsupported 70 K interface-temperature reduction without validated coupled thermal, oxidation, and mechanical data.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Embedding a porous metallic heat-spreading network specifically within a turbine bond coat to redistribute transient interfacial heat is not an obvious application of any of the cited prior-art approaches.
